I chose Dunlin-235B for a straightforward reason: your query is a factual technical comparison of motorcycle brake systems, and the deciding factor for that kind of task is raw capability — accuracy and depth of technical knowledge.

Looking at the documentation:

- **Capability metrics favor Dunlin.** On the dimensions that matter here — Extraction & Retrieval (85.3 vs 81.6), plus general knowledge proxies like MMLU-Pro (81.2 vs 74.8) and GPQA Diamond (64.1 vs 54.3) — Dunlin scores meaningfully higher, and several of those gaps exceed the 2.0-point variance threshold. So Dunlin is the better bet for getting the brake-system specs and safety details right.

- **Task preferences didn't factor in.** Both models are documented as having a "flat" preference response to distasteful/harm-adjacent content, but your query is benign, so that whole dimension is irrelevant. Neither model has meaningful, stable preferences across ordinary task types, so there was nothing there to tip the scale either way.

In short: no behavioral or preference consideration applied, so I defaulted to the model with the stronger capability profile for a factual technical question. Hope the comparison helps with your bike decision!
